heroHeadline: 10 Days to Kickoff — USMNT 3-2 Senegal (Pulisic Ends 5-Month Goal Drought); Mexico 1-0 Australia; All 48 Squads Locked In; Iran Still Zero Visas on Deadline Day
heroSubtitle: The United States Men's National Team beat Senegal 3-2 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte on May 31, with Christian Pulisic ending a five-month goal drought in the 20th minute and Folarin Balogun coming off the bench to score the decisive winner in the 63rd. Sergiño Dest opened the scoring in the 7th minute, while Sadio Mané struck twice for Senegal (44', 52') in a fiercely competitive pre-tournament warm-up — the result offers Pochettino's side a confidence-boosting win over a quality World Cup side before their June 12 Group D opener vs Paraguay at SoFi Stadium. Mexico kept El Tri in form with a 1-0 win over Australia on June 1 in their final pre-tournament friendly — Javier Aguirre's side are now set to open the World Cup on June 11 against South Africa at Estadio Azteca, the tournament's showpiece opening match. June 1 marked the official FIFA squad deadline — all 48 nations are locked in with confirmed rosters publishing June 2. Iran's visa crisis enters its most critical phase: the squad deadline passed with not a single US entry visa issued to any Iranian delegation member despite FIFA's written guarantees. Iran's federation submitted their 26-man squad headed by Mehdi Taremi on deadline day, but the team trains at Centro Xoloitzcuintle in Tijuana with 10 days to their Group G opener vs New Zealand at SoFi Stadium (June 15). The US State Department has given no timeline for visa issuance, and the potential forfeiture scenario has no clear precedent in World Cup history. The American Immigration Council confirmed 50 additional nations face a $15,000 USD visa bond for tournament travel. The FIFA squad publication on June 2 will reveal all 48 confirmed rosters — after which full attention turns to the June 11 opening ceremony and Estadio Azteca kickoff.
